title: Using a linear mixed-effect model framework to estimate multivariate generalizability theory parameters in R
evidence_role: multivariate covariance design and backend eligibility
contract_finding: Fixed dimensions or subtests are not observational facets; covariance structure follows whether conditions are disjoint or shared. The article-era lme4 limitation is outdated for selected random-effect structures in lme4 2.0.6, but the current level-1 residual remains one scale times a known diagonal weight matrix and cannot represent general linked cross-stratum residual covariance.
roadmap_action: Make glmmTMB the conditional general primary route; permit lme4 only when every random block maps to its supported structures and the operational residual is diagonal up to one scale; bind event identity before D-SIM-1.

title: Applying Multivariate Generalizability Theory to Psychological Assessments
evidence_role: decision coefficient and composite weight semantics
contract_finding: G, global D, and cut-score-specific D answer different decisions. Nominal weights express policy importance; effective weights describe realized variance-covariance contributions.
roadmap_action: Keep REL-G and ABS-PHI separate, retain the cut-score non-claim, and prohibit effective weights from replacing frozen nominal policy weights.

title: Customizing Bayesian multivariate generalizability theory to mixed-format tests
contract_finding: Different response formats and facet structures require response-specific families, links, and nonredundant covariance decomposition; an additional residual covariance must not duplicate an observation-event block.
roadmap_action: Keep the Gaussian D-SIM decision layer separate from future ordinal GPCM or GRM likelihoods; admit a Bayesian mixed-format lane only under a new model and prior contract.

title: Does Sparseness Matter? Examining the Use of Generalizability Theory and Many-Facet Rasch Measurement in Sparse Rating Designs
evidence_role: complementary method roles and sparse connectivity
contract_finding: G theory summarizes variance and design dependability, whereas MFR more directly diagnoses individual severity, centrality, and bias. Sparse designs require sufficient connectivity and may reduce diagnostic sensitivity.
roadmap_action: Register MFRM as a nonvoting complementary diagnostic with its own connectivity gate; never treat G theory and MFRM as interchangeable estimators or independent votes.

title: The Dependability of Behavioral Measurements: Theory of Generalizability for Scores and Profiles
evidence_role: foundational multifacet G and D study semantics
contract_finding: The universe of admissible observations, sampled facets, G study, D study, profiles, and weighted composites are distinct. In multivariate studies the variables are fixed, while joint versus independent sampling determines which cross-variable covariance components enter observed scores and differences.
roadmap_action: Retain explicit universe, event linkage, facet-count projection, composite-weight, and decision-family identities; never equate multiple variables with multiple random facets or latent dimensions.

title: A Generalized Partial Credit Model: Application of an EM Algorithm
contract_finding: The GPCM uses an adjacent-category formulation with item discrimination and steps; step order need not be monotone. The fitted application assumes one latent ability and does not turn observational facets into dimensions.
roadmap_action: Preserve the current bounded unidimensional GPCM claim and require an explicit loading map and identification contract before any multidimensional extension.

title: A multidimensional generalized many-facet Rasch model for rubric-based performance assessment
evidence_role: explicit separation of rater facets and latent dimensions
contract_finding: A multidimensional generalized MFRM needs person ability vectors and item-by-dimension discriminations in addition to rater and rubric parameters; location, scale, rater-severity, rater-consistency, and exchangeable-dimension indeterminacy require explicit constraints or postprocessing.
roadmap_action: Treat multidimensional GPCM/MFRM as a separate future model family with loading, rotation or label, scale, connectivity, and recovery gates rather than as an automatic consequence of multiple facets.
